answers.transcript: Vector search alone missed multi-hop questions, for example which supplier ships a part used in a given product. So I kept entities and relations in Neo4j and used Cypher expansion from the entities found in the query, then merged those results with the top-k vector hits and re-ranked them. I built a set of 200 queries with labelled answers. I ran vector-only and hybrid on the same set and compared token-level F1. Hybrid was 2.75 points higher, and most of the gain came from the multi-hop subset. The answer quality went up, but indexing cost went up too.

The latency came from entity extraction at index time. Every chunk went through an LLM call to pull entities and relations before the write to Neo4j. I would batch those calls, cache the extraction for unchanged chunks by content hash, and only re-index the changed documents. None of that touches the 200-query evaluation set, so the F1 comparison stays valid.
It was an API on EC2 behind a load balancer. Files went to S3 and the slow jobs went through a queue to worker instances. If an instance fails, the load balancer stops sending traffic to it.
I think the queue retries the message. I am not sure about the exact settings. For scaling, the ops team set that up, so I do not know what the trigger was.
It was a lot faster after I optimized it. Before, it was slow, and after it handled about ten times more. I do not remember the exact numbers.
I do not remember the batch size. It was on a GPU. We did not have a formal load test, it was from what I saw in the logs.
